── storage ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
  [RISK ] storage.capacity                   provisionable capacity is UNVERIFIED for standard (rancher.io/local-path): the driver publishes no CSIStorageCapacity, there is no OpenEBS DiskPool, and the class is not node-local — required 557 GiB = 200 GiB model weights + 58 GiB platform claims + 269 GiB in-cluster data stores + 30 GiB traces and metrics (30d retention), estimated could be short and the install would fail mid-sync
        budctl will not guess: an unmeasured backend is reported as unknown, not as sufficient
        → check the backend by hand before installing — `vgs` for LVM, `kubectl get diskpool -A` for Mayastor, the cloud console quota for EBS/Azure Disk — and confirm it holds 557 GiB
  [BLOCK] storage.csi-healthy                nothing is registered to provision standard (rancher.io/local-path): there is no CSIDriver object and no pod that answers to that provisioner, so its claims are never acted on
        a class can be created before its driver; the claim then waits forever with no event other than the provisioner name
        → install the CSI driver the class names, or repoint the values at a class whose driver is installed: kubectl get csidrivers
  [PASS ] storage.default-class              default StorageClass "standard" (rancher.io/local-path)
        claims relying on it: microservices.budcache.persistence.className, storage.budappStaticDir.className, storage.budevalDataset.className, storage.budmodelAddDir.className, storage.budmodelRegistry.className
        volumeBindingMode: (unset)
        · kubectl get storageclass
          standard	provisioner=rancher.io/local-path	default=true	expansion=true	binding=(unset)
        does not prove: that a claim in this class binds — only storage.provision exercises the provisioner — nor that it has the capacity storage.capacity sizes
  [PASS ] storage.expansion                  expansion does not apply: every class backing a growth-prone volume is node-local, where the node's disk — not a resizable volume — is the ceiling
        node-local, where allowVolumeExpansion does not apply — each volume is bounded by the disk of the one node it landed on, not by a size that can be resized (storage.capacity measures that disk):
        standard (rancher.io/local-path) backs storage.budmodelAddDir.className, storage.budmodelRegistry.className
        growth-prone volumes: standard is the default, which backs storage.budmodelAddDir.className, storage.budmodelRegistry.className
        · kubectl get storageclass -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,EXPANSION:.allowVolumeExpansion
          standard	provisioner=rancher.io/local-path	default=true	expansion=true	binding=(unset)
        does not prove: that the volumes have room to grow — a node-local volume never moves to a roomier node, and it shares that node's filesystem with the image store; storage.capacity is what measures the free space
  [PASS ] storage.host-prereqs               no candidate StorageClass carries a parameter that implies host-level state
        candidates: standard (the default, relied on by 5 claims)
        does not prove: that the nodes are prepared: a driver can require host state its parameters never name — a kernel module, a device, a mount
  [SKIP ] storage.named-classes              no StorageClass is named in the values (the chart's own defaults); every claim relies on the default, which storage.default-class covers

  [BLOCK] components.dns                     1 of 1 cluster-DNS pod is in kube-system not ready (Running): in-cluster name resolution is failing or one node outage away from it, and every Dapr call, database connection and object-store request resolves through them
        coredns-1 0/0 Running
        → `kubectl -n kube-system describe pod coredns-1` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs coredns-1` — a CrashLooping CoreDNS is usually a bad Corefile, an unreachable upstream resolver in the node's /etc/resolv.conf, or a forwarding loop back into itself. Fix it before installing; nothing in the ApplicationSets can.
        · kubectl -n kube-system get pods (cluster DNS)
          coredns-1 0/0 Running
  [BLOCK] components.ingress                 no running controller could be matched to the IngressClass (traefik (traefik.io/ingress-controller)): if nothing is serving it, every Ingress the install creates stays unclaimed and no hostname the chart publishes answers
        → check the controller is running (`kubectl get pods -A | grep -i ingress`). budctl ties a class to its controller by name, because spec.controller is a vendor identifier with no API link to a workload — so a controller whose pods carry none of those names, or one that runs outside the cluster such as a cloud load-balancer controller, is not matched here, and `domains.inbound-80` / `domains.inbound-443` are what prove that path instead.
        · each IngressClass, and the ready endpoints of the workload its spec.controller names
          ingressclass/traefik controller=traefik.io/ingress-controller -> no workload matched (searched for traefik)
  [PASS ] components.metrics-server          metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1 is served and Available
        backing service: local (served by the API server itself)
        · kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'
          Available=True seeded
        does not prove: an Available APIService does not prove metrics flow for every node: a node whose kubelet the metrics backend cannot scrape still reports `<unknown>` to an HPA, and budctl does not query the metrics API itself.

BLOCKING — the install will fail
  ✗ cluster.installer-rbac
    this identity cannot create namespaces, customresourcedefinitions.apiextensions.k8s.io, clusterroles.rbac.authorization.k8s.io, clusterrolebindings.rbac.authorization.k8s.io, applicationsets.argoproj.io: the bootstrap stops at the first object it applies and nothing installs
    → bind the install identity to a role that grants them — for a POC, `kubectl create clusterrolebinding budctl-installer --clusterrole=cluster-admin --user=<identity>`; for a scoped role, grant create on namespaces, customresourcedefinitions, clusterroles, clusterrolebindings and applicationsets.argoproj.io
  ✗ components.dns
    1 of 1 cluster-DNS pod is in kube-system not ready (Running): in-cluster name resolution is failing or one node outage away from it, and every Dapr call, database connection and object-store request resolves through them
    → `kubectl -n kube-system describe pod coredns-1` and `kubectl -n kube-system logs coredns-1` — a CrashLooping CoreDNS is usually a bad Corefile, an unreachable upstream resolver in the node's /etc/resolv.conf, or a forwarding loop back into itself. Fix it before installing; nothing in the ApplicationSets can.
  ✗ components.ingress
    no running controller could be matched to the IngressClass (traefik (traefik.io/ingress-controller)): if nothing is serving it, every Ingress the install creates stays unclaimed and no hostname the chart publishes answers
    → check the controller is running (`kubectl get pods -A | grep -i ingress`). budctl ties a class to its controller by name, because spec.controller is a vendor identifier with no API link to a workload — so a controller whose pods carry none of those names, or one that runs outside the cluster such as a cloud load-balancer controller, is not matched here, and `domains.inbound-80` / `domains.inbound-443` are what prove that path instead.
  ✗ storage.csi-healthy
    nothing is registered to provision standard (rancher.io/local-path): there is no CSIDriver object and no pod that answers to that provisioner, so its claims are never acted on
    → install the CSI driver the class names, or repoint the values at a class whose driver is installed: kubectl get csidrivers

  ! storage.capacity
